gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 identifies misuse of arc-length measure instead of the complex line element in a complex-layer representation and its jump relation. Gold I001 concerns replacing a tangential exact-differential integral by the normal-derivative flux integral; these are distinct formulas and failed obligations.

ISSUE-003 diagnoses a line-element versus arc-length error in the definition and jump calculation of a complex layer. Gold I002 is a sign error in the quadratic term of f_G and the resulting real-part calculation; the formulas and obligations differ.

Both concern the Steklov numerical construction, but ISSUE-004 identifies omission of the mean-term matrix M from the eigenproblem. Gold I004 concerns the incorrect unweighted transpose identity for D_s and the missing H weights; these are different operator formulas and obligations.

Both address the Steklov discretization, but ISSUE-004 diagnoses omission of the +M mean term in the generalized eigenproblem. Gold I005 concerns double application of quadrature weights in the singular S_1 block, a different matrix formula and discretization obligation.

Both identify that the stated discrete Steklov pencil uses S(I−M) instead of the modified operator S_0=S(I−M)+M, causing the constant-density direction and zero mode to be mishandled. ISSUE-004 gives the corresponding corrected pencil with +M.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The printed Steklov eigenproblem omits the +M term required to discretize S_0, so it represents a different and degenerate pencil that mishandles the constant-density/zero-mode subspace.

component_coverage.gold_component: The discrete pencil uses S(I−M) rather than the stated modified operator S_0=S(I−M)+M, thereby annihilating the constant-density direction and failing to represent the full Steklov problem.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 explicitly states that +Mφ is omitted, describes the resulting degenerate pencil and missing eigenpairs, and supplies the corrected right-hand matrix S(I−M)+M.
